data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) requirements for retaining, maintaining, and allowing access to information system logs.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) requirements for retaining, maintaining, and allowing access to information system logs

policy_statements.source_text: It guides all Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to implement Log Management Infrastructure (LMI), which consists of processes, personnel, and tools.
policy_statements.target: all Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: To ensure USDA complies with Federal requirements to establish, implement, and enforce system activity logging and maintenance of logs that support the Department’s management of information security risks to the USDA enterprise.
policy_statements.target: system activity logging and maintenance of logs that support the Department’s management of information security risks to the USDA enterprise

policy_statements.source_text: This DR addresses and meets the requirements of:
Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) §§ 3551-3559;
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) §§ 3551-3559

policy_statements.source_text: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular No. A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control;
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular No. A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control

policy_statements.source_text: OMB, Circular No. A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource;
cross_references: OMB, Circular No. A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource

policy_statements.source_text: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Improving the Federal Government’s Investigative and Remediation Capabilities Related to Cybersecurity Incidents;
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Improving the Federal Government’s Investigative and Remediation Capabilities Related to Cybersecurity Incidents

policy_statements.source_text: National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST), Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST), Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: NIST, Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations;
cross_references: NIST, Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: NIST, SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management; and
cross_references: NIST, SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management

policy_statements.source_text: Record retention requirements in the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedules (GRS).
cross_references: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedules (GRS)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is effective immediately when published and will remain in effect until superseded or expiration.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their related Information Systems Log Retention policies with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: their related Information Systems Log Retention policies
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: The term “USDA personnel” encompasses USDA employees, contractors, partners, interns, fellows, affiliates, and volunteers.
This policy applies to all:
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and personnel who implement or maintain information systems log retention procedures, plans, and functions;
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and personnel who implement or maintain information systems log retention procedures, plans, and functions
conditions: who implement or maintain information systems log retention procedures, plans, and functions

policy_statements.source_text: Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, processed, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA;
policy_statements.target: Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, processed, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Information systems, and cloud-based services used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: Information systems, and cloud-based services used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: These include interconnections between or among these information systems or services;
policy_statements.target: interconnections between or among these information systems or services

policy_statements.source_text: Facilities from which these systems or services operate, including:
Facilities owned or operated by USDA; and
policy_statements.target: Facilities owned or operated by USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Facilities owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a third party.
policy_statements.target: Facilities owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a third party
conditions: on behalf of USDA by a third party

policy_statements.source_text: This DR sets requirements for information system event logging, management of logs, and maintenance of LMI.
policy_statements.target: information system event logging, management of logs, and maintenance of LMI

policy_statements.source_text: It mandates implementing an LMI to identify and manage risks, consistent with the system categorization.
Nothing in this policy alters the requirements for protecting national security systems or information.
policy_statements.target: requirements for protecting national security systems or information

policy_statements.source_text: This includes those identified in policies, directives, instructions, and advisory memoranda issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) or by the intelligence community.
The planning activities for information system logging, maintenance of system logs, and management of LMI ensure logs are stored in sufficient detail for an appropriate or required period.
Planning activities should properly scope, configure, and implement these capabilities.
The USDA security information and event management (SIEM) system ingests logs from across the USDA enterprise to support investigations, response and recovery efforts.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA security information and event management (SIEM) system
policy_statements.target: logs from across the USDA enterprise

policy_statements.source_text: This DR specifies a model for evaluating the maturity level of system logging and management requirements defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, which establishes requirements for Federal agencies to increase the sharing of log information, to accelerate incident response efforts and to enable more effective defense of Federal information systems and agencies.
policy_statements.target: maturity level of system logging and management requirements defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31

policy_statements.source_text: The LMI can filter, aggregate, normalize, and correlate logs to support event analysis.
Efficient and effective log management balances resources with the required level of log data detail.
The LMI also supports log confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure practices and processes are in accordance with NIST SP 800-92 and OMB, Memorandum M-21-31.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: NIST SP 800-92
OMB, Memorandum M-21-31

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Information Security Center (ISC) logging agent will be the primary logging capability on USDA assets.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Information Security Center (ISC) logging agent

policy_statements.source_text: Auditable security events will be logged to support investigative actions, log review, analysis, and reporting in the USDA Enterprise Logging SIEM system.

The technical logging details in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix C, Logging Requirements – Technical Details, provide the common categories of auditable security events to be considered for mandatory logging and the log thereof retained for required periods of time.
policy_statements.target: common categories of auditable security events to be considered for mandatory logging
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix C, Logging Requirements – Technical Details

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may log additional information for moderate and high-impact systems, to achieve or maintain compliance with Federal log requirements.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will configure systems and tools to collect logs needed to support investigations, event reconstruction, metrics, and research.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that logs have the detail required to facilitate event reconstruction.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will encrypt the LMI and establish access controls in accordance with OMB, Memorandum M-21-31.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that log content for high-impact systems can be configured from a central location, are time-correlated, and implement non-repudiation measures.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The LMI (tools, processes, and personnel) will support log retention requirements, including retention periods specified in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix C.
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix C

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Enterprise Logging SIEM will:
Allocate sufficient storage capacity to support OMB mandates;
Maintain offline back-ups as required in OMB guidance; and
Preserve logs in a manner that allows for centralized access.
The USDA Enterprise Logging SIEM will be configured to:
Overwrite the oldest logs during a log processing failure;
Overwrite the oldest logs when storage capacity is exceeded for high-impact systems and cannot be shutdown based on mission needs or risk to the system; and
conditions: when storage capacity is exceeded for high-impact systems and cannot be shutdown based on mission needs or risk to the system

policy_statements.source_text: Notify the Mission Area, agency, staff office, the USDA OCIO-ISC Security Operations Center (SOC), and other stakeholders of breaches, log failures, or when log storage reaches capacity.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, staff office, the USDA OCIO-ISC Security Operations Center (SOC), and other stakeholders
conditions: of breaches, log failures, or when log storage reaches capacity

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will review, implement, and adhere to the time stamp schema defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix A, Implementation and Centralized Access Requirements.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: time stamp schema defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix A, Implementation and Centralized Access Requirements
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, Appendix A, Implementation and Centralized Access Requirements

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will apply the four-tier event logging (EL) maturity model defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31 to prioritize efforts, resources, and measure the level of compliance with logging and log management requirements.
policy_statements.target: four-tier event logging (EL) maturity model defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31

policy_statements.source_text: The four EL tiers that define compliance with requirements for implementation are:
Tier EL0 has a rating of “Not Effective” indicating that logging requirements of highest criticality are either not met or are only partially met;
Tier EL1 has a rating of “Basic” indicating that only logging requirements of highest criticality are met;
Tier EL2 has a rating of “Intermediate” indicating that logging requirements of highest and intermediate criticality are met; and
Tier EL3 has a rating of “Advanced” indicating that logging requirements at all criticality levels are met.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure log management compliance, prioritizing high-impact systems and high value assets (HVA).
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Per Executive Order 14028, Improving America’s Cybersecurity, and OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, the USDA SOC will share information with the Cybersecurity Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).
policy_statements.target: Cybersecurity Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
cross_references: Executive Order 14028, Improving America’s Cybersecurity
OMB, Memorandum M-21-31

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will document and analyze lessons learned on their programs, control activities, procedures, and tasks.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: lessons learned on their programs, control activities, procedures, and tasks

policy_statements.source_text: They will use this qualitative and quantitative data to assess effectiveness and to guide process improvement.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Ensure the USDA logging and log management program is adequately funded; and
policy_statements.target: USDA logging and log management program

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee the information technology (IT) resources that generate, transmit, and store the logs.
policy_statements.target: information technology (IT) resources that generate, transmit, and store the logs
conditions: that generate, transmit, and store the logs

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) will:
Coordinate with the CIO to ensure implementation of an LMI and compliance with Departmental logging and log management requirements;
Coordinate with Mission Area Assistant CIOs to ensure information systems can perform required logging;
Report to the CIO on the effectiveness of the logging and log management programs, including on violations of policy; and
Review or approve enterprise risks via the Risk-Based Decision (RBD) process.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs will ensure personnel with logging and log management responsibilities complete role-based training.
policy_statements.target: personnel with logging and log management responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CISOs or Information Systems Security Managers (ISSM) will:
Provide guidance for prioritizing the log management requirements and meeting the hardware and software requirements for information systems; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CISOs or Information Systems Security Managers (ISSM)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure required event notifications are accurate and timely.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CISOs or Information Systems Security Managers (ISSM)

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of the OCIO-ISC Cybersecurity Infrastructure Division (CSID) will:
Implement an effective LMI to ensure central logging and secure retention of logs;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director of the OCIO-ISC Cybersecurity Infrastructure Division (CSID)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Log Management Administrators coordinate with System Owners and Information Owners to:
Maintain the LMI;
Identify all systems required to forward logging data; and
policy_statements.target: all systems required to forward logging data

policy_statements.source_text: Configure their system logging functions to provide the required data; and
Manage the validation of logging capabilities to ensure compliance.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director of the OCIO-ISC Cybersecurity Infrastructure Division (CSID)

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of the OCIO-ISC Cyber Defense Operations Division (CDOD) will:
Share information with CISA and the FBI; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Director of the OCIO-ISC Cyber Defense Operations Division (CDOD)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the SOC notifies appropriate stakeholders of log failures or when log storage reaches capacity.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director of the OCIO-ISC Cyber Defense Operations Division (CDOD)
conditions: of log failures or when log storage reaches capacity

policy_statements.source_text: System Owners will:
Ensure information systems integrate with the LMI;
Ensure the preservation of logs to support investigations, response and recovery efforts, and Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests; and
cross_references: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the Information Owner when setting log retention requirements and time periods.
conditions: when setting log retention requirements and time periods

policy_statements.source_text: Information Owners will:
Inform the System Owner of information system log and log retention requirements; and
Coordinate with Log Management Administrators and System Owners to ensure that all required logs are transferred to CDOD.
policy_statements.target: Log Management Administrators and System Owners

policy_statements.source_text: Security Architects or Engineers will:
Provide guidance for LMI solutions such as log collection, storage, and retrieval;
policy_statements.target: LMI solutions such as log collection, storage, and retrieval

policy_statements.source_text: Employ, configure, and test log capabilities; and
Update log procedures, and log configurations as needed.
Log Management Administrators, and System, Database, and Network Administrators will:
Ensure the LMI aligns with OMB, Memorandum M-21-31, and NARA GRS retention requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Log Management Administrators, and System, Database, and Network Administrators
cross_references: OMB, Memorandum M-21-31
NARA GRS

policy_statements.source_text: Configure logging and log management capabilities to collect required data in accordance with authoritative references; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Log Management Administrators, and System, Database, and Network Administrators

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the log failures, security, and storage processes.
policy_statements.actor_name: Log Management Administrators, and System, Database, and Network Administrators

USDA will apply the four-tier event logging (EL) maturity model defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31 to prioritize efforts, resources, and measure the level of compliance with logging and log management requirements.
four-tier event logging (EL) maturity model defined in OMB, Memorandum M-21-31
The four EL tiers that define compliance with requirements for implementation are:
Tier EL0 has a rating of “Not Effective” indicating that logging requirements of highest criticality are either not met or are only partially met;
Tier EL1 has a rating of “Basic” indicating that only logging requirements of highest criticality are met;
Tier EL2 has a rating of “Intermediate” indicating that logging requirements of highest and intermediate criticality are met; and
Tier EL3 has a rating of “Advanced” indicating that logging requirements at all criticality levels are met.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure log management compliance, prioritizing high-impact systems and high value assets (HVA).
